text:
Mathieu Olivier made his name as an enforcer, and The Athletic recently wrote about him trying to get back to that intimidating style while Columbus searches for goals. The odd thing is that his offense has been fine: three goals and six points in 15 games, and a three-point night in the 7-2 win over Colorado.

His ice time is up three minutes over the last ten games, to more than 16 a night, and Columbus has 51% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, better than without him. His three goals came on 4.1 expected, slightly unlucky.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net often last season (84th percentile among forwards) while carrying the puck in on only 28% of his entries, a dump, chase and crash game. He's an undrafted player from Mississippi who scored 15 goals last season. Our projection sees about 20 goals. Not many fighters get that.
